label: thm:df-cf-timesharing
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:df-cf-timesharing}
Consider a primitive diamond relay channel,  every rate $R<r_{\mathrm{D}}+r_{\mathrm{C}}$ is achievable for some nonnegative $r_{\mathrm{D}}$ and
$r_{\mathrm{C}}$ satisfying
\begin{subequations}
\label{eq:df-cf-timesharing}
\begin{align}
    r_{\mathrm{D}}
    &\leq
    \lambda I_{\mathrm{D}}(X;Y_1),
    \label{eq:df-cf-df1}\\
    r_{\mathrm{D}}
    &\leq
    \lambda I_{\mathrm{D}}(X;Y_2),
    \label{eq:df-cf-df2}\\
    r_{\mathrm{D}}
    &\leq
    a_1+a_2,
    \label{eq:df-cf-df3}\\
    r_{\mathrm{C}}
    &\leq
    (1-\lambda)
    I_{\mathrm{C}}(X;\hat Y_1,\hat Y_2),
    \label{eq:df-cf-cf1}\\
    r_{\mathrm{C}}
    &\leq
    C_1-a_1
    +(1-\lambda)
    \bigl[
        I_{\mathrm{C}}(X;\hat Y_2)
        -I_{\mathrm{C}}(Y_1;\hat Y_1|X)
    \bigr],
    \label{eq:df-cf-cf2}\\
    r_{\mathrm{C}}
    &\leq
    C_2-a_2
    +(1-\lambda)
    \bigl[
        I_{\mathrm{C}}(X;\hat Y_1)
        -I_{\mathrm{C}}(Y_2;\hat Y_2|X)
    \bigr],
    \label{eq:df-cf-cf3}\\
    r_{\mathrm{C}}
    &\leq
    C_1+C_2-a_1-a_2
    -(1-\lambda)
    \bigl[
        I_{\mathrm{C}}(Y_1;\hat Y_1|X)
        +I_{\mathrm{C}}(Y_2;\hat Y_2|X)
    \bigr].
    \label{eq:df-cf-cf4}
\end{align}
\end{subequations}
Here, $I_{\mathrm{D}}$ denotes mutual information evaluated
according to a distribution of the form
\[
    p_{\mathrm{D}}(x,y_1,y_2)
    =
    p_{\mathrm{D}}(x)p(y_1|x)p(y_2|x),
\]
whereas $I_{\mathrm{C}}$ denotes mutual information evaluated
according to a distribution of the form
\[
    p_{\mathrm{C}}(x,y_1,y_2,\hat y_1,\hat y_2) =
    p_{\mathrm{C}}(x)p(y_1|x)p(y_2|x)
    p(\hat y_1|y_1)p(\hat y_2|y_2).
\]
It suffices to consider compression alphabets satisfying $|\mathcal{\hat Y}_1|\leq |\mathcal{Y}_1|+3$ and $|\mathcal{\hat Y}_2|\leq |\mathcal{Y}_2|+3$.

The union is taken over all such distributions and all
\[
    \lambda\in[0,1],\qquad
    0\leq a_1\leq C_1,\qquad
    0\leq a_2\leq C_2.
\]

title: Proof
body_md:
The argument follows in the same flavor to the proof of \cite[Proposition~1]{egn21}, with the modifications needed to accommodate the second relay link. We consider the joint distribution $(M,X^n,Y_1^n,Y_2^n,J_{1,n},J_{2,n})$ induced by any given code.

We start with Fano's inequality,
$$nR = H(M)\leq I(M;J_{1,n},J_{2,n})+n\epsilon_n.$$

We identify $U_i =(Y_{2,i+1}^n,Y_1^{i-1},J_{1,n})$, and $V_i = (Y_{2,i+1}^n,Y_1^{i-1},J_{2,n})$. Let $Q$ be a time-sharing random variable uniform on $[1:n]$ and independent of everything else. Further let $U =(Q,U_Q),V=(Q,V_Q), X = X_Q, Y_1 = Y_{1,Q},Y_2=Y_{2,Q}$. 

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{First bound.}
\begin{align*}
    n(R-\epsilon_n) \leq &I(M;J_{1,n},J_{2,n})\leq  I(X^n;J_{1,n},Y_2^n)\\
    =& I(X^n;J_{1,n},Y_2^n)+I(X^n;Y_1^n,J_{1,n})-I(X^n;Y_1^n,J_{1,n})\\
    \overset{(a)}{=}&I(X^n;Y_1^n)+I(X^n;Y_2^n|J_{1,n})-I(X^n;Y_1^n|J_{1,n})\\
    \overset{(b)}{=}&
    \sum_{i=1}^n I(X_i;Y_{1,i}|Y^{i-1})
    +I(X_i;Y_{2,i}|J_{1,n},Y_1^{i-1},Y_{2,i+1}^n)
    -I(X_i;Y_{1,i}|J_{1,n},Y_1^{i-1},Y_{2,i+1}^n)\\
    \overset{(c)}{\leq} &\sum_{i=1}^n I(X_i;Y_{1,i})
    +I(X_i;Y_{2,i}|J_{1,n},Y_1^{i-1},Y_{2,i+1}^n)
    -I(X_i;Y_{1,i}|J_{1,n},Y_1^{i-1},Y_{2,i+1}^n)\\
    =&\sum_{i=1}^n I(X_i;Y_{1,i})
    +I(X_i;Y_{2,i}|U_i)
    -I(X_i;Y_{1,i}|U_i)\\
    = & n\bigg(I(X_Q;Y_{1,Q}|Q)
    +I(X_Q;Y_{2,Q}|U_Q,Q)
    -I(X_Q;Y_{1,Q}|U_Q,Q)\bigg)\\
    \overset{(d)}{\leq}&n\bigg(I(X;Y_1)+I(X;Y_2|U)-I(X;Y_1|U)\bigg).
\end{align*}
Here $(a)$ uses $J_{1,n}= f_{1,n}(Y_1^n)$; $(b)$ follows by the telescoping sum and the Csisz\'ar--K\"orner--Marton sum identity; $(c)$ drops $-I(Y_i;Y^{i-1})$; $(d)$ holds since $Q\rightarrow X_Q\rightarrow (Y_{1,Q},Y_{2,Q})$ is Markov.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Second bound.}
\begin{align*}
    n (R-\epsilon_n)\leq & I(M;J_{1,n},J_{2,n})\leq I(X^n;J_{1,n},Y_2^n)\\
    \overset{(a)}{=}& I(X^n;Y_2^n)+I(X^n;J_{1,n}|Y_2^n)+H(J_{1,n}|Y_1^n,X^n,Y_2^n)\\
    =&I(X^n;Y_2^n)-I(J_{1,n};Y_1^n|X^n,Y_2^n)+H(J_{1,n}|Y_2^n)\\
    \overset{(b)}{\leq} &nC_1+ I(X^n;Y_2^n)-I(J_{1,n};Y_1^n|X^n)\\
    \overset{(c)}{=}&nC_1+\sum_{i=1}^n I(X_i;Y_{2,i}|Y_{2,i+1}^n)-I(J_{1,n};Y_{1,i}|X^n,Y_1^{i-1})\\
    \overset{(d)}{\leq } &nC_1+\sum_{i=1}^n I(X_i;Y_{2,i})-I(J_{1,n};Y_{1,i}|X^n,Y_1^{i-1})\\
    \overset{(e)}{\leq}&nC_1+\sum_{i=1}^n I(X_i;Y_{2,i})-I(J_{1,n},Y_1^{i-1},Y_{2,i+1}^n;Y_{1,i}|X_i) 
    \\
    =&nC_1+\sum_{i=1}^n I(X_i;Y_{2,i})-I(U_i;Y_{1,i}|X_i) 
    \\
     =&nC_1+n\bigg( I(X_Q;Y_{2,Q}|Q)-I(U_Q;Y_{1,Q}|X_Q,Q)\bigg)\\
    \overset{(f)}{\leq}&nC_1+n\bigg( I(X;Y_2)-I(U;Y_1|X)\bigg).
\end{align*}
Here $(a)$ again uses $J_{1,n} =f_{1,n}(Y_1^n)$; $(b)$ holds by $H(J_{1,n}|Y_2^n)\leq H(J_{1,n})\leq C_1$; $(c)$ follows by the Csisz\'ar--K\"orner--Marton sum identity; $(d)$ drops $-I(Y_{2,i};Y_{2,i+1}^n)$; $(e)$ follows by the Markov chain conditions $(Y_1^{i-1},X^{n\setminus i})\rightarrow X_i\rightarrow Y_{1,i}$, $Y_{2,i+1}^n\rightarrow (J_{1,n},Y_1^{i-1},X^n)\rightarrow Y_{1,i}$, and dropping $I(X^{n\setminus i}; Y_{1,i}|J_{1,n},Y_1^{i-1},Y_{2,i+1}^n,X_i)$; $(f)$ holds since $Q\rightarrow X_Q\rightarrow (Y_{1,Q},Y_{2,Q})$ is Markov.
 
\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Third and fourth bounds.}
Exchanging the roles of the two relays (i.e.\ interchanging the indices $1\leftrightarrow2$,
replacing $U$ by $V$) in the two chains above gives
\begin{align*}
    n(R-\epsilon_n)\leq & n\bigg(I(X;Y_2)+I(X;Y_1|V)-I(X;Y_2|V)\bigg),\\
    n(R-\epsilon_n)\leq& nC_2+n\bigg(I(X;Y_1)-I(V;Y_2|X)\bigg).
\end{align*}
\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Fifth bound.}
\begin{align*}
    n(R-\epsilon_n)\leq& I(M;J_{1,n},J_{2,n}) \leq I(X^n;J_{1,n},J_{2,n})\\
    \leq& I(X^n;J_{1,n})+I(X^n;J_{2,n})\\
    \overset{(a)}{\leq} & nC_1+nC_2-H(J_{1,n}|X^n)-H(J_{2,n}|X^n)\\
    \overset{(b)}{=} &nC_1+nC_2-I(J_{1,n};Y_1^n|X^n)-I(J_{2,n};Y_2^n|X^n)\\
    \overset{(c)}{=}&nC_1+nC_2+\sum_{i=1}^n-I(J_{1,n};Y_{1,i}|X^n,Y_1^{i-1})-I(J_{2,n};Y_{2,i}|X^n,Y_{2,i+1}^n)\\
    \overset{(d)}{\leq }&nC_1+nC_2+\sum_{i=1}^n-I(J_{1,n},Y_1^{i-1},Y_{2,i+1}^n;Y_{1,i}|X_i)-I(J_{2,n},Y_1^{i-1},Y_{2,i+1}^n;Y_{2,i}|X_i)\\
    =&nC_1+nC_2+\sum_{i=1}^n-I(U_i;Y_{1,i}|X_i)-I(V_i;Y_{2,i}|X_i)\\
    =&nC_1+nC_2+n\bigg(-I(U_Q;Y_{1,Q}|X_Q,Q)-I(V_Q;Y_{2,Q}|X_Q,Q)\bigg)\\
    \overset{(e)}{=}&n\bigg(C_1+C_2-I(U;Y_1|X)-I(V;Y_2|X)\bigg).
\end{align*}
Here $(a)$ follows by $H(J_{1,n})\leq C_1$ and $H(J_{2,n})\leq C_2$; $(b)$ follows as $J_{1,n} = f_{1,n}(Y_1^n)$ and $J_{2,n} = f_{2,n}(Y_2^n)$; $(c)$ uses the telescoping sum; $(d)$ follows by the Markov chain conditions $(X^{n\setminus i},Y_1^{i-1})\rightarrow X_i\rightarrow Y_{1,i}$, $Y_{2,i+1}^n\rightarrow (J_{1,n},Y_1^{i-1},X^n)\rightarrow Y_{1,i}$, $(X^{n\setminus i},Y_{2,i+1}^n)\rightarrow X_i\rightarrow Y_{2,i}$, $Y_1^{i-1}\rightarrow (J_{2,n},Y_{2,i+1}^n,X^n)\rightarrow Y_{2,i}$, dropping $-I(X^{n\setminus i}; Y_{1,i}|J_{1,n},Y_1^{i-1},Y_{2,i+1}^n,X_i)$, and dropping $-I(X^{n\setminus i}; Y_{2,i}|J_{2,n},Y_1^{i-1},Y_{2,i+1}^n,X_i)$; $(e)$ holds as $Q\rightarrow X_Q\rightarrow (Y_{1,Q},Y_{2,Q})$ is Markov. 

Letting $n\to\infty$ so that $\epsilon_n\to0$, and invoking continuity of the
mutual-information terms in the induced joint distribution, gives the five claimed constraints.

The cardinality bounds $|U|\leq |X||Y_1|+1$ and $|V|\leq |X||Y_2|+1$ are due to the standard Caratheodory-Bunt\cite{bunt1934bijdrage} arguments.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
After some elementary manipulation, the five constraints in Theorem~\ref{ob:relayuvw} can be rewritten as
\begin{align*}
        R\leq &I(X;Y_2)+C_1-I(U;Y_1|X),\\
        R\leq &I(X;Y_2,Y_1)-I(U;Y_2|Y_1)-I(X;Y_1|U,Y_2),\\
        R\leq & I(X;Y_1)+C_2-I(V;Y_2|X),\\
        R\leq & I(X;Y_2,Y_1)-I(V;Y_1|Y_2)-I(X;Y_2|V,Y_1),\\
        R\leq &C_1+C_2-I(U;Y_1|X)-I(V;Y_2|X).
    \end{align*}
By non-negativity of mutual information terms, the upper bound in Theorem~\ref{ob:relayuvw} is at least as tight as the cut-set bound for the general primitive diamond relay channel.

body_md:
Suppose we have $\{a_j^A\}, \{a_j^B\}\in \mathcal{A}$, and $P^A,P^B\in \mathcal{P}$, such that $a_j^A\leq F_j(P^A),a_j^B\leq F_j(P^B),\forall j\in[1:5]$. 
        
        Let $Q\in \{A,B\}$ be Bernoulli($\theta$). We construct a new distribution $r((u,q),(v,q),x)$ such that $\forall (u,v,x)\in\mathcal{U}\times\mathcal{V}\times \mathcal{X}$,
        \begin{align*}
            r((u,A),(v,A),x) =& \theta p^A(u,v,x), \\
            r((u,B),(v,B),x) =& (1-\theta)p^B(u,v,x).
        \end{align*}
        $r\in\mathcal{P}$ since $(U,Q)\rightarrow (X,Y_1)\rightarrow Y_2$, $(V,Q)\rightarrow (X,Y_2)\rightarrow Y_1$, and the power constraint holds as follows
        $$\mathbb E_r[X^2] =\theta \mathbb E_{p^A}[X^2]+(1-\theta) \mathbb E_{p^B}[X^2]\leq P.$$

        In the following, we demonstrate $F_j(r)\geq \theta a_j^A+(1-\theta)a_j^B$ for $j=1,2,5$. The argument for $j=3,4$ follows analogously. Thus, $\mathcal{A}$ is convex.
        \begin{align*}
            F_1(r) =& I_r(X;Y_2)+C_1-I_r(U,Q;Y_1|X)\\
            =&I_r(X;Y_2|Q)+C_1-I_r(U;Y_1|X,Q)+I_r(Q;Y_2)-I_r(Q;Y_1|X)\\
            =&I_r(X;Y_2|Q)+C_1-I_r(U;Y_1|X,Q)+I_r(Q;Y_2)\\
            \geq &I_r(X;Y_2|Q)+C_1-I_r(U;Y_1|X,Q)\\
            =&\theta (I_{p^A}(X;Y_2)+C_1-I_{p^A}(U;Y_1|X))+(1-\theta) (I_{p^B}(X;Y_2)+C_1-I_{p^B}(U;Y_1|X))\\
            =&\theta F_1(p^A)+(1-\theta )F_1(p^B)\\
            \geq &\theta a_1^A+(1-\theta)a_1^B.\\
            F_2(r)=&I_r(X;Y_1)+I_r(X;Y_2|U,Q)-I_r(X;Y_1|U,Q)\\
            =&I_r(X;Y_1|Q)+I_r(X;Y_2|U,Q)-I_r(X;Y_1|U,Q)+I_r(Q;Y_1)\\
            \geq &I_r(X;Y_1|Q)+I_r(X;Y_2|U,Q)-I_r(X;Y_1|U,Q)\\
            =&\theta (I_{p^A}(X;Y_1)+I_{p^A}(X;Y_2|U)-I_{p^A}(X;Y_1|U))+(1-\theta) (I_{p^B}(X;Y_1)+I_{p^B}(X;Y_2|U)-I_{p^B}(X;Y_1|U))\\
            =& \theta F_2(p^A)+(1-\theta) F_2(p^B)\\
            \geq & \theta a_2^A+(1-\theta)a_2^B.\\
            F_5(r)=& C_1+C_2-I_r(U,Q;Y_1|X)-I_r(V,Q;Y_2|X)\\
            =&C_1+C_2-I_r(U;Y_1|X,Q)-I_r(V;Y_2|X,Q)-I_r(Q;Y_1|X)-I_r(Q;Y_2|X)\\
            =&C_1+C_2-I_r(U;Y_1|X,Q)-I_r(V;Y_2|X,Q)\\
            =&\theta (C_1+C_2-I_{p^A}(U;Y_1|X)-I_{p^A}(V;Y_2|X))+(1-\theta) (C_1+C_2-I_{p^B}(U;Y_1|X)-I_{p^B}(V;Y_2|X))\\
            =&\theta F_5(p^A)+(1-\theta) F_5 (p^B)\\
            \geq & \theta a_5^A+(1-\theta) a_5^B.
        \end{align*}

title: Remark
body_md:
In a similar way, we can prove the set $\mathcal{A}^G:=\{a\in \mathcal{R}^5:a_j\leq F_j(p)\quad\forall j, \text{  for some }p\in \mathcal{P}^G \}$ is convex, where
        $\mathcal P^G$ denotes the subset to  $\mathcal{P}$ with additional requirements such that $P_X$, $P_{X,Y_1|U}$, $P_{X,Y_2|V}$ are Gaussian. Moreover, we conclude the following min-max exchange:
$$\max_{p\in \mathcal{P}^G}\min_{\substack{\lambda_j\geq 0,\\\sum_{j=1}^5 \lambda_j=1}} \sum_{j=1}^5 \lambda_j F_j(p)
        =\min_{\substack{\lambda_j\geq 0,\\\sum_{j=1}^5 \lambda_j=1}} \max_{p\in\mathcal{P}^G} \sum_{j=1}^5 \lambda_j F_j(p).$$
